title: driver-sql: on an upgraded MySQL 8 database the widening arm never accepts a functional-digest package-less guard, so the old narrower unique is kept and a second package's row of one name is refused
body:
domain:server#7 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibzKCovWpJoMZD6U3NT

Filing gate: ① product defect, located by reading the code with its mechanism written down (reach: a named real producer, `driver-sql`'s widening arm, on every MySQL 8 database upgraded from a release that had the narrower key). Found by the red-line read of #33199 (round-1 design finding M4), declared there as a limit.

## Business rationale

Who: an operator running on MySQL 8.0.13+ who upgraded a database created before ADR-0150 widened three platform keys to carry the package. What breaks: the old, narrower unique key is never retired, so the database keeps refusing exactly what the widening exists to admit:

- `sys_user_permission_set` (#32164): one user cannot hold two packages' permission sets of one name in one organization.
- `sys_connector_connection` (#33199, #31699): one organization cannot connect two packages' connector instances of one name.
- `sys_metadata_activation` (#31682): read from the same code; the activation ledger's MySQL guard takes the same functional form, so the ledger's old `(metadata_type, name)` key is kept too. Not measured.

Each is unreachable while the phase-1 one-holder backstop keeps a name to one package, and becomes a refusal the user cannot get past (no prescription names it) once ADR-0150's narrowing lands for that type. SQLite, PostgreSQL, MariaDB 10.3+ and MongoDB retire the old key; a database created fresh on MySQL never has it. If not fixed: MySQL deployments silently keep phase-1 behaviour for these tables after the platform moves on.

## Mechanism

- The guard on MySQL is a UNIQUE key over a functional key part, the driver's hash-shadow digest, NULL for a packaged row (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/*-packageless-index.ts`, MySQL branch).
- Introspection records that key part as an expression (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-introspection.ts`, the `EXPRESSION` branch of the MySQL statistics read).
- `hasPartialUniqueGuard` (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts`) accepts only `partial === true` with no expressions, so the guard never counts, and `widenedUniqueReplacements` keeps the old key (`kept`), with no plan op ever offered.
- Pinned as the declared limit in `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-widened-connection-key.test.ts` (MySQL cell: no index op, a second package's row refused).

## Acceptance

- `driver-sql` recognises the platform's MySQL functional-digest guard (the digest expression over exactly the narrower columns, NULL when the gained column is non-null) as a partial unique on those columns, so the arm plans the same safe `replace_unique_index` as on PostgreSQL.
- The MySQL cells of the three widened-key suites flip from the declared limit to the replace; MariaDB unchanged.
- The declared-limit sentences go (changesets of #32164 and #33199 are released text; the new changeset says FROM kept TO retired, plus `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` "Runtime-owned indexes apply builds").

## Who acts

The server lane's `driver-sql` owner, as one PR after #33199 lands (it adds the connection table's MySQL cell this card flips). Not folded into #31699: it is a driver change across three tables.

## Duplicate search

`gh api search/issues` over this repo, issues: `hasPartialUniqueGuard` 2 hits (#31699, #32164, neither tracks it); `MySQL functional key part guard` 26 (#31732 is the MongoDB analogue, closed; none for MySQL); `widening arm MySQL` 228, first page none; `packageless MySQL expression` 4, none.
